title: Button fallback story and soft-disabled state polish
creator: Maya Chen
description: Polish and document a resilient fallback story for button tokens and introduce a 'soft-disabled' visual state for transient, cancelable actions. This ticket covers: token fallback rules when semantic tokens are missing or overridden, icon-only spacing regressions across themes, spinner overlap/escape hatch behavior, motion-reduction-safe micro-interactions, and final acceptance criteria for engineering handoff. Goal is to reduce visual regressions observed after token migration and make disabled feedback more informative without blocking cancelable flows.
background_and_rationale: Several regressions were reported after the token migration: icon buttons losing hit-target padding in high-contrast themes, spinners overlaying labels in compact variants, and hard-disabled states preventing graceful cancellation patterns in forms. We need a design-level fallback contract so engineers can implement deterministic behavior when tokens are absent or when customers override semantic palettes. In parallel, product asked for a 'soft-disabled' state for actions that are temporarily unavailable but cancelable (e.g., network retry pending). This reduces user confusion compared to the existing opaque disabled style.
acceptance_criteria: Define token fallback priority list (semantic -> alias -> core) and publish mapping table in Confluence
Add 'soft-disabled' visual spec: silhouette + reduced opacity + retain focus ring + show cancel affordance (where applicable)
Icon-only buttons keep minimum 40px tap target across all themes and densities; verify in Figma components and snapshot tests
Spinner placement rules: never overlap label baseline; spinner may replace leading icon or shift to trailing edge depending on variant
Provide CSS token examples and engineering notes for theme handover and token override points
Design review completed and signoff from accessibility reviewer stating color contrast >= 4.5:1 for interactive states (except when overridden with documented warning)
Design assets (Figma), a gesture spec, and a single reference PR in the component library exist for implementation
implementation_notes: Create a fallback mapping file: --fallback-order: semantic, alias, core; engineers to read on component init
Soft-disabled should be a separate CSS modifier (--soft-disabled) so it can be toggled without affecting aria-disabled semantics
Icon-only spacing: introduce --icon-padding token and ensure it resolves to min(12px, floor(available/4)) for responsive layouts
Spinner behavior: prefer inline replacement of leading icon for primary/ghost variants; for compact variants, move spinner to trailing position to avoid label shift
Motion: provide reduced-motion variants that replace transforms with opacity transitions; provide test harness for QA
Add a non-blocking telemetry metric for 'soft-disabled' cases to product analytics to track user cancellations
design_decisions_and_tradeoffs: We intentionally keep soft-disabled keyboard focusable to allow users to cancel or regain control; tradeoff: potential accidental activation if engineers do not wire cancel affordance
Token fallback favors semantic tokens to preserve designers' intent; if missing, alias fallback may change color slightly — documented as acceptable for legacy themes
Spinner placement rules prefer visual stability over minimal layout shift; this means in some edge widths the icon may disappear then reappear after load
We avoid introducing a new API surface on the Redwood Button props for every edge case; instead prefer CSS tokens + a single 'softDisabled' boolean prop that maps to tokens
